miniProject.title: Correctness-first harness with timelines, counters and regime evidence
miniProject.brief: Harden the kernellab harness: a manifest with machine state, paired interleaved trials with raw samples, independent references over an adversarial matrix, four sanitizer reproducers, minimal counter captures, a roofline point, three classified regimes and an end-to-end bound with retained losses. Counter steps run under `sudo ncu` or record the permission block with counter-free evidence.
steps: Extend `manifests/env.json` with a timestamped machine-state log: SM clock, power and temperature from `nvidia-smi -q -d CLOCK,POWER,TEMPERATURE`, background processes, whether clocks can be locked without privilege, and allocator behavior. Run one short timing twice with interleaved variants, attach both logs, and write an interference and isolation audit that explains any state difference without attributing every fluctuation to one cause. Add the rotating-buffer cache experiment: fresh-process first call against rotating preallocated inputs against reused inputs, with warmup samples kept and the preserved state declared for each.

Implement paired randomized interleaved trials in `harness/run.py` with a recorded seed, raw per-trial samples, a drift plot and a documented resampling unit with uncertainty. Show the method on synthetic paired latencies baseline `[10, 20, 30]` against candidate `[5, 10, 15]`: both medians and paired speedups give 2, and perfectly proportional pairs can resample with zero spread without proving noise-free hardware. Apply the same summaries to retained interleaved GPU samples from two seeded 512 by 512 `torch.float32` matmuls on the RTX 3050 (10 warmup, 20 timed) with event and synchronized host boundaries and a CPU double-precision check of the last output.

Write independent copy and reduction references in `refs/` that share no logic with the kernels. Cover lengths 0, 1, 31, 32, 33, 255, 256 and 257, a stride-two view of a known sequence at zero tolerance with every element compared, and output prefilled with `NaN` so omitting the last element fails; the empty path must avoid an invalid zero-block launch. Keep seeded tail and stride regressions, then add cancellation, `NaN`, infinity, overflow, underflow and all-masked policy tests with a stated tolerance rule. Run the four CS336 accumulation loops unchanged on CPU and explain them: 10.000133514404297 and 9.953125 for the fp32 and fp16 loops, 10.00213623046875 for both fp32-accumulated loops as 1000 times the fp16 value 0.01000213623046875, separating input rounding from accumulation rounding.

Seed four minimal reproducers in `kernels/cuda/diag/`: a one-past-the-end write, an uninitialized global read, a shared-memory neighbor read without a barrier, and `__syncwarp(0x0000ffff)` called by all 32 threads of a warp. Build the first three for `sm_86` with `-lineinfo` and run `compute-sanitizer --tool memcheck --padding 32`, initcheck and racecheck so each reports its defect; build the last with `-G` so synccheck reports Barrier error detected with invalid arguments while an `-O3` build reports nothing because the compiler removed the barrier. Keep each log, repair and regression test.

Capture one NVTX-annotated `nsys profile --trace=cuda,nvtx --sample=none --cpuctxsw=none` timeline for the matmul batch, follow one API call to its kernel, identify the final synchronization and report the union of kernel intervals beside the event interval and completed wall time. Then take a minimal hypothesis linked `sudo ncu` capture requesting only `LaunchStats` plus one section, recording replay mode, pass count, cache and clock control and observer overhead against unprofiled time. Where counters are denied, keep the `ERR_NVGPUCTRPERM` record and substitute event timing plus `cuobjdump -res-usage` and occupancy API evidence with no overhead ratio claimed.

Derive the operation and byte model for out-of-place fp32 scaled vector addition with a register scalar: \(F = 2n\) and minimum requested bytes \(Q = 12n\) for intensity \(I = 1/6\) FLOP/byte, with streaming no-reuse bound \(t\) above \(\max(2n/P, 12n/B)\). Place one event-timed point with useful FLOPs and modeled bytes labeled, using sourced or calibrated ceilings, and add traffic-counter checks only where permitted; without counters never call \(12n/t\) measured DRAM bandwidth.

Predeclare three regimes with one falsifier each: a tiny copy as launch sensitive, a streaming copy larger than L2 as bandwidth sensitive, and a GEMM size sweep as compute sensitive. Collect interleaved event timings, a timeline and static launch and resource evidence, adding minimal counter sections only under `sudo ncu` where permitted. Report each hypothesis as confirmed, contradicted or unresolved rather than forcing all three labels when evidence is incomplete.

Apply the end-to-end bound \(T_{e} = T(1-f+f/s)+d\): for a synthetic 100 ms workload with a 40 ms kernel at speedup 2 the total is 80 ms (1.25x), and 85 ms near 1.176x with 5 ms of dispatch and conversion. Apply the same formula with critical-path share to one retained trace, report kernel time beside completed invocation latency across the shape matrix including retained losing shapes, and file a device-scoped reproduction manifest. Include the CS336 memory note as a labeled observation: one full AdamW step on the small model at batch 4 peaked at 2.93 GiB at context 256, 4.83 at 512 and 10.74 at 1024, with medium at 8.41 and 13.55 GiB at 256 and 512 and OOM at 1024 on 24 GB.
deliverables: The hardened harness with the machine-state log, paired interleaved trials, raw samples, drift plots and the rotating-buffer cache evidence.
Independent references with the adversarial matrix, seeded tail and stride regressions and the extreme value policy beside the four-loop numerical note.
Four sanitizer reproducers with logs, repairs and regressions; one `nsys` timeline with NVTX correlation; one minimal `sudo ncu` capture or the permission-block record with counter-free evidence.
The roofline point with labeled models and ceilings, three regime reports with falsifiers, and the end-to-end bound with losing shapes and the reproduction manifest.

checks.name: CS336 Assignment 2 local tests
checks.note: Run the `benchmarking_script`, `nsys_profile`, `mixed_precision_accumulation` and `memory_profiling` problems locally on sizes that fit 6 GB.

rubric.pass: Independent references pass the full length matrix and stride-two views at stated tolerance, seeded tail and stride regressions fail on the seeded omission, and extreme inputs follow the written policy.
rubric.strong: The four-loop note separates input rounding from accumulation rounding with the exact values quoted.

rubric.pass: Each reproducer reports under its stated tool and flags, the `-G` synccheck case and the `-O3` silence are both kept, and the timeline attributes one host gap or transfer without reaching for counters first.
rubric.strong: Regressions are minimal single-defect programs with the exact log line that identifies each defect.

rubric.pass: The `sudo ncu` capture is minimal and hypothesis linked with replay and overhead recorded, or the permission block is kept with event plus `cuobjdump -res-usage` evidence, and each regime carries a falsifier and a verdict of confirmed, contradicted or unresolved.
rubric.strong: The roofline labels useful against requested against actual bytes and never claims measured bandwidth without traffic counters.

rubric.pass: The bound is applied with critical-path share, kernel time sits beside completed invocation latency, losing shapes are retained, and the manifest scopes reproduction to one device.
rubric.strong: The report states which invocation costs the kernel win cannot move.

miniProject.feedsInto: Capstone laboratory: the harness, references, sanitizer regressions, timelines, counters and regime evidence. Later kernel sections reuse the trial design and the bound.
